newsitem.title: UK: Oxford Instruments down after H1 figures.
newsitem.headline: Oxford Instruments down after H1 figures.

text.p: Shares in Oxford Instruments Plc dropped on Thursday amid talk of analyst downgradings after the company posted slightly disappointing first-half results.
The shares were down at 21-1/2p at 470p by 1526 GMT with less than 70,000 shares changing hands.

"What happened is that analysts believe the company's profit will be lower next year than they had previously expected," said one analyst, who asked not to be named. "It's a matter of lower expectations."
Oxford Instruments, which researches and makes advanced instrumentation, posted a 5.5 percent rise in first-half pre-tax profits to 9.53 million stg from 9.03 million a year ago.
Turnover rose 2.3 percent to 67.0 million stg.
"The result is a little bit disappointing and the sales figures are low," said another.
In a statement chairman Peter Williams said both its principal groups of businesses, instrumenation and superconductivity, performed well and were in line with expectations.
He said new orders rose to record levels and the annual rate of order intake was running at 166 million stg, up nearly 10 percent on the start of the year.
